narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 28% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The prediction was shaped most by three key factors. First, you’ve never failed a class before, which is a strong positive sign—most students who pass also have a clean record here. Second, your father is listed as your guardian; while this isn’t unusual, the model noticed that students with a mother as guardian tend to have slightly better outcomes, so this slightly increased the concern. Finally, you’ve expressed a clear desire to pursue higher education, which actually works in your favor—it shows motivation and aligns with students who typically succeed.

Other details also played a role. For example, your parents’ education level is lower than most of your peers, and you don’t have internet access at home, which may limit some resources. However, you study between 2 and 5 hours a week, which is about average, and your family relationships are good. The model also noted that you don’t take extra paid classes or participate in many extracurricular activities, which could be areas to explore for additional support.

The remedial courses are an opportunity to strengthen your skills and confidence. Focus on consistent study habits, and consider reaching out to teachers or counselors for extra help in areas where you feel less confident. Your goal of higher education is still very much within reach—this is just a step to help you get there.
